verdict.rationale: Foreloop accepts plain-language problem statements as the start of work, and its agent turns them into intentions and proposed tasks (foreloop-docs-4, foreloop-docs-12, foreloop-docs-35). Natural-language operation of the product itself is only indirect: it goes through external agents such as Claude Code or Codex, which use its MCP endpoint or the agent-friendly CLI (foreloop-docs-3, foreloop-docs-5, foreloop-docs-16). The only in-product commands shown are fixed-syntax @foreloop comment commands (foreloop-docs-24, foreloop-docs-26). Missing for 10: a first-party natural-language command or chat interface for operating the product, documented examples of driving projects and tasks in natural language through MCP, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
